title: Closed subsets are cut out by quasi-coherent ideals
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $Z\subseteq Y$ a closed subset. There exists a quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent] sheaf of ideals $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ whose vanishing set $V(\mathcal J)=\{y\in Y:\mathcal J_y\neq\mathcal O_{Y,y}\}$ is $Z$.

source.place: Schemes Lemma 01J3 (schemes-lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), proof constructs the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf defining a closed subset

proof.text: Apply the existing reduced-induced-closed-subscheme construction [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] to $X=Y$ and $T=Z$. Its sheaf $\mathcal I_Z$ is quasi-coherent, and on every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ it is the radical ideal $I$ with $V(I)=Z\cap U$. The associated closed subscheme has image $Z$, so the stalk vanishing locus $V(\mathcal I_Z)=Z$. Taking $\mathcal J=\mathcal I_Z$ gives the required quasi-coherent ideal sheaf.
